title: Here’s Where Our Memories Go as We Age
author: Jake Currie
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPsychologyHere’s Where Our Memories Go as We AgeIt’s more nuanced than you thinkJCBy Jake Currie7:00 AM CDT on August 24, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleYour memory is going to change as you get older, even if your brain stays healthy. Your recall might get slower, names and dates might become more slippery, and you might struggle to recall some events. It’s just a fact of life. Now a new study published in Psychology and Aging is painting a more nuanced picture of age-related memory loss. Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 10 See Blue Origin Crew's Amazing View Of Earth In NS-36 Launch HighlightsShareNextStayPsychologists from the University of East Anglia in the United Kingdom rounded up 37 young adults (between the ages of 18 and 33) and 37 older adults (between the ages of 60 and 85) to test their memory recall. The two groups were asked to recount either specific episodic memories or more repeated categoric memories in as much detail as possible after being prompted by cue words. For example, if the cue word was “karaoke,” a specific memory might be, “I got drunk at a karaoke bar last weekend and embarrassed myself singing ‘Sweet Caroline,’ but the crowd loved it,” while a categoric memory might be, “When I do karaoke, my go-to songs are anything by Neil Diamond because we have the same range, and I usually stick to beer to keep my pipes lubricated.” Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
